questions.stimulus: Many residents believe the new bike lane has reduced car traffic. But traffic counts show car volume is unchanged. So the bike lane has not reduced car traffic.

clauses.text: Many residents believe the new bike lane has reduced car traffic.
But traffic counts show car volume is unchanged.
So the bike lane has not reduced car traffic.

questions.explanation: Opening tell: 'Many residents believe' flags an opposing view. The 'But' pivots to the author. The 'So' delivers the author's main conclusion.

questions.stimulus: Some critics have argued that ranked-choice voting confuses voters because ballot complexity rises with each new option. Yet exit polls in three pilot cities show that more than 90% of voters reported the ballot was easy to understand. Ranked-choice voting does not confuse voters.

clauses.text: Some critics have argued that ranked-choice voting confuses voters
because ballot complexity rises with each new option
Yet exit polls in three pilot cities show that more than 90% of voters reported the ballot was easy to understand
Ranked-choice voting does not confuse voters

questions.explanation: 'Some critics have argued' marks opposing-view territory. The 'because' clause is opposing evidence supporting that opposing conclusion. The 'Yet' pivots to the author, whose evidence is the exit-poll data.

questions.stimulus: Although the company posted record revenue last year, its operating margins fell to a five-year low. When margins fall while revenue rises, the underlying business is usually weakening. The company is in trouble.

clauses.text: Although the company posted record revenue last year
its operating margins fell to a five-year low
When margins fall while revenue rises, the underlying business is usually weakening

questions.explanation: 'Although' opens a concession. The author admits the good news, then pivots to their own evidence (the margin decline) plus a general principle. The conclusion comes last.

questions.stimulus: Coastal wetlands buffer cities from storm surges. Recent zoning changes have permitted residential development in several wetland zones. While developers argue that the new homes generate badly needed property-tax revenue, the long-term flood damage avoided by intact wetlands exceeds any plausible tax gain. The zoning change is a mistake.

clauses.text: Coastal wetlands buffer cities from storm surges
Recent zoning changes have permitted residential development in several wetland zones
While developers argue that the new homes generate badly needed property-tax revenue
the long-term flood damage avoided by intact wetlands exceeds any plausible tax gain
The zoning change is a mistake

questions.explanation: First two clauses set neutral background. 'While developers argue' introduces an opposing view. The author's evidence is the cost-benefit comparison, and the last sentence is the main conclusion.

questions.stimulus: It is widely believed that the average commuter saves money by driving rather than taking transit. However, a recent study calculating fuel, insurance, depreciation, and parking costs found that driving is more expensive than transit in seven of the ten largest U.S. cities. The conventional wisdom is wrong.

clauses.text: It is widely believed that the average commuter saves money by driving rather than taking transit
However, a recent study calculating fuel, insurance, depreciation, and parking costs found that driving is more expensive than transit in seven of the ten largest U.S. cities

questions.explanation: 'It is widely believed' is the opposing-view flag. 'However' pivots to the author, whose evidence is the study. The author's conclusion arrives last.
